question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights will be void?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 13,** is the only option that **directly mentions laws inconsistent with or in derogation** of fundamental rights.
 
• Article 13 states that any law that is inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights shall be void.
 
• It** ensures that laws that conflict with fundamental rights are void to the extent of their inconsistency.**
 
• It **establishes the supremacy of the Constitutio**n and safeguards citizens against arbitrary legislative actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 15**:

 
 
• It **Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth**.
 
• It ensures equality before the law and equal protection within the territory of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 14:**
 
 
• It **Provides the right to equality before the law **and equal protection of the laws within India.
 
• It forms the basis for non-discrimination and equal opportunity.
 
 
 
• **Article 16:**
 
 
• **It ****Guarantees equal opportunity for all citizens in matters of public employment or appointment** to any office under the State.
 
• It also prohibits discrimination in matters of employment on grounds such as religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
